assigned.title: notFound() never reaches the wire: dead addresses answer 200
assigned.notes: IMPLEMENTED IN THE TREE AND NEVER CLAIMED, like the rest of recovery packet 1 -- but PARTIALLY, and the two gaps are different in kind. This is the fifth task found in that state, and its code landed while it sat BACKLOG and unowned: control/events.jsonl records apps/web/src/app/loading.tsx and page.tsx being edited as belonging to PL-0704 while it was blocked on a lifecycle dependency. So it must be started with --reconcile-existing, never against HEAD. IT IS A MODIFICATION TASK IN THE REVIEWER'S TAXONOMY, MOSTLY, and that changes the probe. Its central act was a DELETION -- the root loading.tsx removed -- and marker absence cannot witness a deletion. What it also did, and what CAN be witnessed, is introduce two named components where anonymous route-level skeletons used to be: CatalogSkeleton in app/page.tsx and PlaybackLoading in app/watch/[contentId]/page.tsx, each now a Suspense fallback sitting BELOW the existence decision rather than a loading file wrapping the whole segment. Those two names are new even though their markup is not, so a pickaxe on the names finds the relocation, which is precisely this task's work. Use them as the witnesses; do not use the deleted file. TWO GAPS AGAINST THE ACCEPTANCE, AND ONLY ONE IS A CODE GAP. FIRST, THE TITLE SKELETON, WHICH I BELIEVE IS A CONTRACT GAP RATHER THAN A DEFECT AND AM FLAGGING FOR A RULING RATHER THAN FIXING. The acceptance says any fix must KEEP the loading skeletons rather than deleting them to move a status code. Home and watch comply: both relocated their skeleton into a Suspense boundary below a cheap existence check that consults nobody. The title route did not -- it deleted its skeleton outright -- and its own header argues why: on that route a status line precedes the first body byte, so no byte may be sent before the catalog answers whether the title exists, which is the definition of having nothing to stream. A full-page skeleton there IS the defect the task exists to remove. The only honest way to restore one would be a section whose data does not depend on the title existing, and none exists today. So the code looks right and the clause looks over-general. I am not rewriting the acceptance to match the code unasked -- that is the move the reviewer has twice had to authorise explicitly, on PL-0205's wording and on PL-0706's -- so it is proposed here and left for the verdict. SECOND, THE PRODUCTION-MODE 404, WHICH IS NOT THIS TASK'S TO CLOSE. An unknown title answers 404 under development and 200 with a refusal panel under production, and that is correct rather than broken: on a hosted build no catalog metadata source is constructible, so loadTitleDetail reports error rather than not-found, notFound() is unreachable, and a build that answered 404 there would be claiming an absence it never looked for. The precondition is a catalog source that exists in a deployment, which is PL-0305's, now READY since PL-0105 completed. ALLOWEDPATHS CORRECTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. apps/web/src/app/(home)/** is DROPPED: it is a dead declaration for a route-group approach that was considered and rejected, it reserves a directory that does not exist, and it starves nothing only by accident. apps/web/src/app/loading.tsx is KEPT even though the file is deleted, because the deletion is the change and a surface that omitted it would not fingerprint the task's central act. TWO PATHS ADDED. docs/E2E.md, because it and .github/workflows/ci.yml currently CONTRADICT EACH OTHER about whether the two 404 assertions have ever been observed passing -- E2E.md claims an executed 2026-09-05 pass on all four browser projects, ci.yml says UNKNOWN, expected to pass, never observed passing -- and settling that is exactly what this task's EXECUTED clause is about. It is declared by PL-0706, which is DONE, and by PL-0703, which is BLOCKED, so no active conflict. And .github/workflows/ci.yml, which UNTIL NOW WAS DECLARED BY NO TASK IN THE REPOSITORY AT ALL: every CI change this project has made has landed outside every declared surface. That is a real declaration hole rather than a convenience, and this task adopting it is a partial fix at best -- the file is repository governance rather than frontend, and it should eventually belong to whatever task adopts CLAUDE.md and control/README.md, which are undeclared for the same reason.
assigned.acceptance: An unknown title id and a malformed watch id each answer HTTP 404 rather than a skeleton served at 200, proven by an EXECUTED Playwright run rather than by a route calling notFound(). The cause is that a segment's loading file wraps that segment in Suspense, so React flushes the shell at 200 before the access-fallback error escapes the render and Next can set the status; the root loading file wraps every route in the application, so per-route fixes alone are insufficient. Any fix must keep the loading skeletons rather than deleting them to move a status code. DEPENDS ON PL-0103 because the title route is that task's declared write surface and it is currently in REVIEW; this is a lifecycle dependency, not a technical one.

PL-0704's own additions in this count are a fourth case in apps/web/src/app/watch/route-loading-boundaries.test.ts asserting that the two relocated skeletons still exist -- that CatalogSkeleton is still defined in app/page.tsx and still rendered as a Suspense fallback, and the same for PlaybackLoading in app/watch/[contentId]/page.tsx. It was confirmed non-vacuous by temporarily swapping the home fallback to null, which produced the intended named failure, and the pre-existing guard in the same file was confirmed non-vacuous by recreating a trivial root loading.tsx, which produced two named violations.

e2e.evidence: EXECUTED Playwright run, not a prediction, which is the clause this task exists to satisfy. From e2e/ after npm ci in that directory, exit 0. Development: LIBERTY_E2E_WEB_MODE=development npx playwright test --project=api --project=chromium at 82a50dc, exit 0, 43 passed 3 skipped 0 failed. Production, the default: npx playwright test --project=api --project=chromium at 82a50dc, exit 0, 34 passed 12 skipped 0 failed. Specs: catalog.api, playback-session.api, progress.api, rights-boundary.api, critical-journey, search, media-rig skipped for no rig. The asserted statuses: critical-journey.spec.ts:448 for /title/no-such-title-pl0701 expects 404 under development and passed, and expects 200 with catalog_source_not_configured under production and passed; critical-journey.spec.ts:750 for /watch/Not%20A%20Valid%20Id expects 404 and passed in BOTH modes; critical-journey.spec.ts:814, the new skeleton-retention case, passed in both modes. Served bytes carried no Loading title and no Loading player on the 404 cases. Second independent witness, not the spec reading itself: the dev server request log recorded GET /title/no-such-title-pl0701 404 in 140ms and GET /watch/Not%20A%20Valid%20Id 404 in 71ms, and a separate curl probe of an independently started next dev returned 404, 404, 200, 200, 200 for the unknown title, malformed watch id, real title, real watch id and root. ONE NARROWING OF THIS EVIDENCE, STATED PLAINLY RATHER THAN OMITTED: the browser under test was NOT the pinned revision. The container ships Chromium revision 1194, Chromium 141.0.7390.37, while @playwright/test 1.62.1 requires 1234, and the first attempt failed verbatim with browserType.launch: Executable doesn't exist at /opt/pw-browsers/chromium_headless_shell-1234/chrome-headless-shell-linux64/chrome-headless-shell. playwright install was unavailable. Rather than edit e2e/playwright.config.ts, which is outside this task's allowedPaths, a symlink registry presenting the 1194 build under the 1234 names was built in a scratch directory and selected with PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH; nothing in the repository changed for it. That is exactly the drift the pinning comment in playwright.config.ts exists to prevent, and it is recorded in docs/E2E.md as well as here. Only the api and chromium projects ran -- the pair CI runs -- so this says nothing about WebKit, mobile-safari or Firefox, and PL-0705's WebKit clause is untouched. No claim is made that the CI job will be green: a container run is not that job, and asserting otherwise would be the same class of claim as the expected to pass comments this task deleted.

implementationBaseProvenance.reason: The base is f6c4b942ebbd02fd3fa9ed8f74fde4fc603affc2, the first parent of 719d2d7c31465901f3dbee1e936a180e87c3d44f, derived from history rather than named: 719d2d7 is the one commit that deletes all three loading files, retires HomeLoading and WatchLoading, and introduces CatalogSkeleton and PlaybackLoading, and 'git grep <Suspense> f6c4b94 -- apps/web/src/app' returns only a prose comment, so not one Suspense boundary of this task's arrangement existed in the base tree under any name or in any file. Because the two named witnesses are relocations and could have carried the PL-0205 risk, they are backed by that structural absence, by the paired disappearance of HomeLoading and WatchLoading in the same commit, and by route-loading-boundaries.test.ts being a genuine add there -- the only renames in this repository are PL-AI-0006's four packages/contracts moves, outside this surface. The whole declared surface was swept rename-aware with --full-history plus --follow on the five leaf paths and a conservative 13-file enumeration of title/** and watch/**, reconstructing the deleted apps/web/src/app/loading.tsx deliberately; that yields exactly 23 pre-base commits, every one pre-existing work: c9efc49, 5399c92 and 4091a2b build the three loading files that are the defect, ba2bf47 writes the two 404 assertions as PL-0701's acceptance harness twelve days before this task existed, 8b1172b is the first executed run, which created PL-0704 in control/tasks.json and states in the code that the fix is not done here, and c469e92 adds the comment DO NOT DELETE THIS TO RECOVER THE 404 ... The status is PL-0704's to fix, in the root file. The two document paths were proven separately because that is what sank PL-0601 and PL-0401: .github/workflows/ci.yml contains no 404, loading, skeleton or PL-0704 text whatsoever at the base and gains the entire 404 CI record at 719d2d7, while docs/E2E.md carries only 8b1172b's failing-run report whose prescribed route-group remedy this task rejected rather than implemented. The probes were proven before use, reproducing gpt-architect's own PL-0603 re-derivation exactly and reproducing the three-deletions-one-survivor loading-file set recorded in control/events.jsonl. ONE CLASSIFICATION IS LOAD-BEARING AND IS FLAGGED RATHER THAN BURIED: ba2bf47 and 8b1172b put this task's exact subject matter on its declared e2e and docs paths before the base. They are classified as the task's input rather than its implementation, because ba2bf47 predates PL-0704's existence in control/tasks.json by twelve days and was written by PL-0701's harness lane as an expected-to-pass assertion, and 8b1172b is the commit that created PL-0704, says in the code being changed that the fix is not done here, and proposes a route-group remedy PL-0704 recorded as considered and rejected. If the reviewer rules that authoring a deliberately-red acceptance assertion is part of delivering that acceptance, this base moves and this derivation is wrong.
